Lounge, Crescendo, Drift, Cosmic, Betelgeuse). Each went through the scene plan (`--schedule ... --cues`, section 60)
in a fitting preset, once with the cues and once from the audio alone. The cues mark where every section starts and
where the drops land, so they serve as the answer key.

**With cues, the scenes were already right.** In Club, Psytrance and Electronic every cue section got its change
within 0.1 s, and every cue drop got its drop cut. Calm presets take a section as a natural change after 20 s, so
there a cue often falls into a running 6-25 s fade or the 20 s stay. That is intended.

**But the cues reached only the scene cut.** Three things were missing:

- *The drop's hit.* The drop pulse -- the shaders' `audioDrop` (74 scenes), the present pass's streaks, the shock
  wave and the drop rewind -- and the phrase grid's anchor came from the analyser alone, even with cues live. The
  analyser missed both drops of Uplifting, so its drops cut without a hit. In Goa it took the build-up after the
  break for a drop, and the hit came 12 s early.

  Now `RenderPipeline::conditionAudio` drains the cues once a frame, before the conditioner (`buildSchedulerTick`
  reads the same frame). While cues are live:
  - the conditioner's drop count and drop pulse are the cues' (the pulse decays like the analyser's, 0.66 s);
  - the analyser's guesses are ignored;
  - the count carries on across the switch-over, so neither direction reads as a drop;
  - a cue bar line resets the bar position and snaps the phrase grid's integrated beats to the bar, so the grid
    cannot drift.

  The plan now also records the picture's drop hit (`hit` rows: the conditioned pulse crossing 0.85). With cues every
  drop hit came 0.02-0.08 s after the cue drop, and none came anywhere else. Goa's false hit is gone.

- *The kind of section.* A break got the same 0.8 s hard cut as a drop. Now `applyScoreCues` sets
  `Tick::sectionFalls` when the new section is calmer than the last: a Break, Cut or Outro, or 0.15 less energy. The
  scheduler then takes the change as a natural one ("music-soft"):
  - on the next downbeat (the cue's bar line), without waiting for the phrase;
  - faded over 8 to 16 beats (3.3-8 s in the demos), floored by the transition's own minFade.

  The overlay follows the same rule. The hard cut stays the drop's gesture. `check_schedule` checks that a soft
  change lasts at least eight beats.

- *Tested.* `Kaleidoscope.exe -q` gains five checks for `sectionFalls` (127 pass). `check_schedule --quick` and a run
  with Riot's cues in Club, Psytrance, Ambient and Downtempo show no violations.

**The analyser without cues, measured.** The family's demos with cue files are a labelled test set for the
analyser: 43 tracks, 281 section boundaries, 30 drops. `Tools/analyser_vs_cues.py` (new) runs every one through
`PresetEditor --features` and counts:

| | found | invented |
|---|---|---|
| section boundaries | 106 of 281 (38 %) | 159 of 259 (61 %) |
| drops | 6 of 30 (20 %) | 18 of 24 (75 %) |

Found by kind: breaks 73 %, drops 46 %, outros 38 %, grooves 31 %, builds 14 %. Many of the "drops" are not EDM drops
at all: a cinematic climax, a ritual groove's return.

The false drops had three causes:
- 7 of the 18 fell in the intro, between 12 and 24 s. There the bass comes and goes against a slow average that has
  not seen a groove yet.
- 4 came from the return-after-breakdown path where a build-up, not a drop, follows the break (Goa 133 s).
- The rest were orchestral swells.

The bass-gap path now arms only after 30 s, not 12 s. False drops fell from 18 to 10, while the 6 found drops stayed.
The real tracks in `.screen/music` (Astrix, Daft Punk, DMT, Infected Mushroom, Prodigy, ...) and the structure track
keep every drop at the same time.

The rest is left as found and needs its own round:
- the return path that cannot tell a build-up from a drop;
- the trance drop without a bass gap (Uplifting);
- the section detector's 38 %.

The benchmark is the baseline any such change has to beat. With a generator's cues, all of this is moot: the cues
now steer the cut and the hit alike.

## 22.10.2026 (62): the audio analysis, measured against an answer key and rebuilt where it failed

The user asked to optimise the audio analysis. It was measured first, against three sets.

- **The answer key: 43 demos of the generator family.** Each comes with the score cues its generator wrote: every
  section with its kind, every drop, every beat (`Tools/analyser_vs_cues.py`; `@list` freezes a set, since new demos
  keep arriving in `G:/Tools/VRAudio`).
- **Seven real tracks and the structure track.** Their drops were labelled by hand from the bass envelope: the
  moment the bass returns in full after a gap. Their tempo was checked against an autocorrelation over the whole
  track.
- **Four ambient pieces.** They must stay quiet.

For quick iteration a Python prototype rebuilt the analyser's 32 log-spaced bands (FFT 2048, hop 480). Its copy of
the old section detector found 109 boundaries and invented 161; the C++ original found 106 and invented 159. So the
prototype could be trusted as a bench.

### Drops: the bass back at its groove level

The old detector had two paths:
- the bass slamming back to 1.45 x a slow average that froze in the gap, armed by `buildUp > 0.45`;
- the level mix coming back after more than 6 s under its 8-s mean.

It found 6 of the 30 cue drops, with 10 of its 16 drops false. On the real tracks it found none of the 8 labelled
drops and fired 9 times beside them. The level path fired where a break *ended*: at the build-up after it, or while
the music thinned out toward it. Examples: Astrix in the full groove (184.5 s; the drop is at 199), Daft Punk 15 s
early, Prodigy in the middle of the break. The slam path waited for a build-up that the breakbeat demos never
reached.

In the numbers, a dance drop looks like this:
- the bass falls 30-75 dB first;
- it comes back by 20-48 dB within a tenth of a second;
- it returns to its *groove level*, the loudest 2-s bass of the last 45 s.

The new detector (`AudioAnalyzer::processBlock`, "Drop: the bass back at its groove level") has two paths that end
on the same edge: the 60-ms bass within 3 dB of the groove level.
- **A, after a gap:** the bass 30 dB under the groove for at least 6 s. A breakdown often has the build-up inside
  it; the gap counts until the bass is back in full.
- **B, after a vacuum:** the bass 45 dB under the groove for at least 0.25 s, while a build-up is armed. These are
  the beats struck out right before the drop, as in the structure track and many psytrance drops.

The bass is the lowest eight of the 32 bands (40-180 Hz). The groove level is kept as the maxima of 90 half-second
slots. Not before 30 s, at most one every 8 s, and all times in seconds, not blocks. A 480-sample block is 10.9 ms at
44.1 kHz, so in blocks the 6.2-s gap before Astrix's drop counted as 5.7 s and the drop was lost.

|  | cue drops found (+-0.3 s) | false of all | real + structure found | false |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 6 of 30 | 10 of 16 | 3 of 11 (the structure track only) | 9 of 12 |
| after | 16 of 30 | 11 of 27 | 11 of 11 | 2 of 13 |

None fire in the ambient pieces. The other 14 cue drops have no bass return at all (a cinematic climax, a ritual
groove's peak, +-1 dB), so no bass detector can find them.

### Tempo: the autocorrelation gives the number, the kicks the metre

The published tempo was within 4 % of the cues' beats (both folded to 70..180) in 34 % of the rhythmic time. The kick
tempo (`ioiPeriod`) stood whenever the kicks explained their intervals, and wandered wherever they are syncopated: a
breakbeat at 125 read 125..137, a lounge groove at 90 read 92..179. Meanwhile the autocorrelation held 125.0, and when
it was confident it was right 70 % of the time.

Now the autocorrelation sets the tempo when it is confident. The kicks only choose the metre: where they explain
their intervals and sit at a simple ratio to it (2, 1/2, 3/2, 2/3), the tempo is the autocorrelation's times that
ratio. That keeps the synthetic two-step at 174 against an autocorrelation of 116.6.

Result: 34 % -> 54 % of the rhythmic time, 28 % -> 42 % of all. On the real tracks:
- Kadafi 145 -> 121 (the whole-track autocorrelation says 120);
- Prodigy 133.4 -> 130.6 (130);
- Daft Punk now holds 121-125 instead of 121-133.

Left as found:
- slow music (60-90 BPM) read at double tempo: the cues' own metre convention and the prior around 120 disagree;
- Ironic at 3:2.

### Sections: the log shape, two windows, relative to the music's own novelty

The old detector compared a 2.5-s and an 18-s EMA of the *linear* band shares. The bass ruled them: a hat, a pad or a
lead coming in hardly moved the cosine. At the missed boundaries the novelty reached a median of 54 % of the
threshold, while the invented ones sat just above it. And its threshold was absolute. Inside one track the novelty
separated boundaries from the rest well (AUC 0.80-0.94 for breakbeat, psytrance, techno and trance), but across
genres hardly at all (0.73): cinematic and ritual music move ten times as much between their sections as a techno
groove does.

Now, every 0.1 s, the last 3 s are compared with the 12 s before them. The features are the 32 bands' log shape (dB,
its mean removed) plus the loudness, each difference measured in the earlier window's own spread (a two-sample test).
That novelty is read against its median of the last minute (AUC 0.79 across all). A change needs 3 x the median and
1.0 absolute, with 12 s between changes.

Tried and dropped:
- bar-synchronous windows (no gain);
- chroma and onset density (no gain);
- a lower threshold (more found, but twice the detections).

The drop now wins over the section:
- A change is published one frame (0.1 s) after it is found, unless a drop came in between.
- After a drop the section detector rests 12 s. On the structure track, section and drop fell into one block, and the
  plan counted section cuts where the drop's own cut, with its spectacle scene, belonged.

What the scheduler cuts on, a section or a drop, against every cue boundary:

|  | boundaries met | events invented | events |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 110 of 281 (39 %) | 165 of 275 (60 %) | 275 |
| after | 125 of 281 (44 %) | 132 of 252 (52 %) | 252 |

Build-up boundaries are now met in 51 % of cases (14 % before). The four ambient pieces of the drift fix (16.10.2026)
keep 0-2 sections each, and the real tracks keep about as many as before. `Kaleidoscope.exe -q`: 127 of 127.
`check_schedule --quick`: no violations, and the drop cuts on the structure track are back (Club 217, 206 before
the round). The analysis costs the same: 5.5 s for 494 s of audio.

## 23.10.2026 (63): the areal 400 -- twenty labs, forty chain classes, 340 scenes

The list of 23.10.2026 (`docs/proposals-2026-10-23-flaechig-400.md`) asked for areal methods that use the photos
heavily: the photo as fabric, as plate, as relief, as signal. All of it is built, in families A to Z, one commit each.

**A. Twenty labs** (`Tools/scenegen/src/*Lab.glsl`: BandLab, SeparationLab, PartitionLab, TwinPhotoLab, FlowPaintLab,
DiffractionLab, AtlasLab, EngravingLab, ExposureLab, PerceptionLab, MeterLab, FoldLab, MicroscopeLab, LayerCutLab,
TimeChainLab, StripLab, GlassLab, MirrorBilliardLab, DefectLab, SequenceLab). A lab is not a picture but a vocabulary:
`labWalk(seed, ivec4 n, period)` (gen.py `LAB_LIB`) walks through combinations of up to four slots, one slot changing
at a time with a cross-fade (`LAB_FADE` 0.2); the clock is `0.9 sceneAdvance + sceneTime / 75`, and a new section
(`audioSectionId/Prev/Age`, 8 s) draws everything anew. `labPinA..D` pin a slot (1 + class) for tests. The twenty labs hold
22,139 combinations of slot entries (108 for DefectLab up to 10,000 for BandLab), before knobs and photos.

**B. Forty chain classes** for the four stages of the flat chain labs (`chain_lib7.glsl`, copied into gen.py by
`sync_lib7.py`, wired by `patch_r7.py`, listed in `chain_classes.py`; `chain2d_probe.py` -> `Engine/chain2d_classes.tsv`).
The six mirror nets of the list are not reflection groups and became continuous folds (dragon, Gosper, Fibonacci,
Thue-Morse, Cantor, tent, cat, KIFS, Whitney, polar tent). The 43 functions needed their Doxygen in the generated pass
shaders: `Tools/glsl_doc_table.py` now has their entries (the pass generator strips comments, the table gives them back).

**Shared libraries in gen.py** (appended where a source calls them):
- `FRAC_LIB` (family D): `fracTrap/fracZoom/fracCompose` and the complex helpers; the photo is the orbit trap, only the
  first hit counts (later hits wash the photo out), the background is the plain photo, the zoom shallow.
- `LIC_LIB` (H): `licSmear(p, t, len, ch)` -- fourteen dithered steps along the scene's own `licVel(p, t, ch)`.
- `EXPO_LIB` (J): `expAccum(p, t, mode, lodk)` along the scene's `expPath(p, u, t)`: a mean, a lighten stack that picks
  the colour-weighted brightest reading (luma x (0.3 + 2 sat)), or a comet.
- `RHY_LIB` (L): `rhyBeat()/rhyBar()/rhyPhrase()` (a steady clock stands in where the tempo is unknown), `rhyBump(x, at,
  n, w)` (a smooth bump on a cycle), `rhySecBlend/Prev/Cur`. A rhythm scene uses periodic functions of these phases only,
  so nothing jumps at the end of a beat, a bar or a phrase.
- `LIC_LIB` and `EXPO_LIB` come **after the scene's helpers, before `main()`**: the library calls the scene's `licVel` /
  `expPath`, and a prototype in the library made Doxygen merge the two functions' @param lists.

**State scenes** (`//@state W H RATE [32]`): seven rhythm scenes keep averages over the bars in a small field (onset
energy per step and track, the counted beats modulo 35, the tempo from the beat wraps, the smoothed sub-bass), five
scopes count histograms of the photo in a field (waveform, parade, vectorscope, gradient roses, a histogram terrain),
and ten fields with memory are PDEs guided by the photo (wave tank, eikonal fronts, Schroedinger packet, sandpile,
coherence diffusion, chemotaxis, FitzHugh-Nagumo, KPP fronts, dielectric breakdown, stable fluids).
- **PresetEditor does not step state fields**: its renders show the initial field (ones, in some cases). State scenes
  were checked in the app (`ns_sample.py`), the rest in PresetEditor sheets (`sheet.py`).
- Physarum agents do not fit a field, so PhysarumPhotoNetwork is the Keller-Segel chemotaxis model (which forms the same
  kind of network) and PhotoGapFingering a dielectric-breakdown growth instead of Saffman-Taylor's front.
- The stable-fluids flow has two halves in one texture (velocity and pressure | the photo's coordinates carried by the
  flow); the coordinates relax toward their own place so the photo stays recognisable.

**Honest substitutions.** G: five tilings of the list were not feasible as tilings (Spectre, Sphinx, Voderberg, Gosper
island, Pinwheel) and became RhombilleTumbleTiles, DinRectangleBisection, LogSpiralCellCarpet, FractalShoreCells and
RotatedQuadNest.

**Traps of the round.**
- Large heredocs in bash fail with ENAMETOOLONG; a long source goes in with the Write tool. Heredocs also eat backslashes
  (a patch script with regular expressions: Write tool).
- A knob must not be called `screenP` (a function of that name exists); `dot`, `cross`, `round`, `step` and `patch`
  are taken, too.
- `finish_block.py` with every built frag unregistered fails the shader check until all are registered.
- The shake scan reads a local named `pitch` as frame geometry on `audioMelodyPitch`: smoothing in a state field is fine,
  but the name `mel` avoids the false hit.
- A fix of a `.txt` source draft is not a fix of `src/*.glsl` until `mk.py` has run again, and the commit script adds
  what the registration wrote: build, register, commit, in that order.

**The close.**
- *Catalogue:* `render_catalog_export.py` rendered the frames of the 360 new scenes (20 labs, 340 scenes) in 8.8 minutes
  (two jobs, 60 scenes a chunk); `make_catalog.py` over `scan` + `fxscan` -> 2175 scenes, 6803 frames.
- *Ratings:* the ratings given while building were far above the old rows again (interest 6.78 against 5.44, galerie 7.24
  against 4.88). The 340 scenes were set to the old rows' level column by column (the order inside the batch kept; mean
  and spread of each of the eleven columns moved): interest 4.78, galerie 6.24, psychedelic 5.54, electronic 4.21,
  psytrance 4.54. The twenty labs keep 7 to 9 like the older chain labs. RgbParadeCascade lost one step (its three
  channel colours are the one rainbow the catalogue check found). Anchor sheets: `rate_sheet400.py` with the 37 anchors.
- *Measured:* `screen.py --scenes <360> --chunk 60`: 360 windows in 6.8 minutes. Merged into `.screen/` as before
  (`merge_screen.py`), 5248 metric rows and 2175 costs. The new scenes cost 0.60 ms a frame at 1080p in the median
  (the old ones 0.47), the dearest 1.55 ms (IsophoteSilkStreaks, ExposureLab); none above 3 ms (16 of the old ones).
  The state scenes are cheap because the field steps at its own rate (the dearest, PhotoGeodesicFronts at 600 steps a
  second, stays under 0.8 ms).
- The screening flagged one scene as still: VectorscopeBloom only turned with the music's phase and the screening track is
  quiet for its first half. It now turns steadily and breathes by 8 %, and measures 0.041 spatial std (0.0014 before).
- `sync_scene_measures.py` wrote gpuMs and the measured restlessness into Komplett.xml (Spearman 0.99 against the
  hand-set values over all 2175 scenes), `make_genre_configs.py` rebuilt the presets (Allround 2390 entries, Psychedelic 928,
  Club 590, Ambient 784). `check_schedule.py --quick`: 20 plans, no violations.
- *Doxygen:* 470 warnings at first, all from the round-7 chain functions and the two libraries with a prototype; none now.
- *Snapshots:* `scene_snapshots.py render 2026-10-23-flaechig400 --jobs 3`: 2390 frames, two runs (the first was cut at the
  background shell's 30 minutes; its last three entries read FAIL only because of the cut and were rendered by the
  second run: 922 rendered, 0 failed). Against `2026-10-22-base400` (rendered 17:54-19:10 on 22.10): 2030 compared, 217
  changed, 360 new, 0 gone, 27 black as before (0 newly black, no new scene black), 5 unstable.
  - 192 of the 217 changed scenes had a changed file since that set, mostly the dark-scene lift of the same evening
    (famExpose, `b9628517`); the other 25 are simulations that evolve differently (Murmuration, CyclicAutomatonSpirals,

- *PDF:* the portable Chrome printed it only at the second try, with its own `--user-data-dir`, `--virtual-time-budget`

## 23.10.2026 (64): a hundred variants for every new chain class and every lab class

Asked after (63): "can you get a hundred variants for each of the new labs and chains?" Done as parametric variants: a class
keeps its shape and takes its constants (frequencies, rates, offsets, counts, sizes) from a variant number 0..99. Variant 0 is
always the look the class had before.

**Chain classes (40 of round 7).** `chain_lib7.glsl` holds `gVar/gVa/gVb` (the variant's hash and its eight pseudo-random
numbers), `vr(j)`, `vv(j, lo, hi)` (a constant in a range, the middle for variant 0) and `vk(j, n)` (a choice 0..n-1, the
first for variant 0), and `chainSetVar(v, k)`, which turns the stage's sub-variant `v` (0..1) into the variant `floor(100 v)`.
Each of the stage functions of the four chain lab sources and of FxChain calls `chainSetVar(v, k)` after `k = ord?(k)`, and the
pass generator (`make_chainpass.py`) puts it in front of every class pass (`cls(uv, v)`), so the app's per-class passes get the
variants without a new program: the sub-variant that the walk already sets (`closedClass` keeps it across a class change) now
picks the constants. The 40 functions use `vv/vk` for the constants that make the class look different: a tilt, a rate, the
number of arms, a swapped axis, the width of a lens. Where the first sheets showed variants too alike (Veselago lens,
cylinder lens, Maxwell fish eye, lower mirage, Lamb-Oseen row, Faraday waves, Airy packet, capillary waves, Cantor mirror,
rose fold) the ranges were widened or a structural choice was added. Doxygen: the three globals have entries in
`Tools/glsl_doc_vars.py`, the helpers in `glsl_doc_table.py`.

**Labs (20).** `LAB_LIB` (gen.py) has `gLabV[4]` next to `gLabK[4]`: `labWalk` draws a variant 0..99 for every slot and epoch
(`labVar(slot, epoch, seed)`, blended with the class like the classes themselves are), and a look function takes `ivec4 kv`
with the variants of its slots. The constants of the look are `lv(vi, j, lo, hi)` (a range, the middle for variant 0) and
`lk(vi, j, n)` (a choice, the first for variant 0); `j` is a stream number so that the constants of one look are drawn
independently. Rules kept while patching the 20 sources: the middle of every range is the old constant (so variant 0 renders
exactly like the old lab), counts that sit on a seam (arms, sectors, turns of an atan) stay whole numbers, and the encoding
of an inverse (a colour model's encode and decode) uses the same constants on both sides. Test pins: `labPinA..D` pin a class
(1 + class), `labPinV` the variants: 1 + v for all four slots, or 1000 (1 + slot) + 1 + v for one slot alone, the others at
variant 0 (the check sheets have one row per class and the variants in the columns).

**Checks.** Contact sheets (one row per class, the variants 0, 7, 15 ... 95 as columns, the other three slots at their first
class and variant 0; `PresetEditor --render` with the pins) for all 40 chain classes (stage by stage in ChainLab2D, the other
stages off) and for every slot class of the 20 labs (427 classes, 100 variants each: 42,700 lab variants, 4,000 chain
variants). *Variant 0 equals the old look:* all 397 lab rows rendered against the committed (HEAD) frag, the largest mean
deviation of a frame 0.0004 (floating-point noise). *No flat or dark cells.* *Alike:* two metrics (mean difference of the
variants at 56 x 32 and at 224 x 126 pixels; the fine one is the fair one for line and dot textures such as EngravingLab).
Of 83 rows that looked alike at first, 28 are clearly distinct after the second pass (ranges widened, the middle kept), 28 are
subtle (0.005 .. 0.03 against 0.05 .. 0.2 for the strong ones: overlays, seams, overprints, kernels) and 23 have no constants
and stay identical across the hundred: the neutral classes ("none", "plain", "average", "sharp focus") and a few choice classes
(TwinPhotoLab roles 0 and 1, SeparationLab screen "none"). Context matters: a colour model of SeparationLab only shows with a
screen, the illumination of MicroscopeLab only with a directional method, so a row that is inert in the test can act in a walk.
*Cost:* the labs' GPU time at 1080p, measured in the app (`screen.py --scenes`, the 20 labs): median 0.51 ms, the dearest
0.87 ms (LayerCutLab); the values of the first measurement summed 14.9 ms for the twenty and the new ones 10.9 ms, so the
constants did not make the labs dearer (run-to-run differences of the machine are of that size: LayerCutLab 0.65 -> 0.87,
ExposureLab 1.55 -> 0.69). The pass shaders compile as
before; `shadercheck.py` skips the monolithic ChainLab2D in the cold-compile rule (it runs as passes in the app; the editor still
compiles all classes of its first view in 9 to 10 s). Doxygen 0 warnings.

## 23.10.2026 (65): 300 new scenes and 100 new transitions from other fields' operators

Asked after (64): "can we get another 300 scenes, and maybe 100 new transitions (many slow ones that can be used in an ambient
context)? Does your imagination still suffice? As before: full frame, music reactive, in steady motion, rather abstract, and
may use the textures." The list is `docs/proposals-2026-10-23-300-szenen-100-uebergaenge.md` (25 scene families A to Y and
the transition families Z1 to Z8; the Stand paragraph there says what was built). The answer to the imagination question
was yes, but the free space had moved: motifs ("one more neon flight, one more fractal") are used up, **operators from other
fields** are not. Of the first 350 ideas about 50 existed in substance already (found by name and by keyword search in the
descriptions of all 3226 entries); they were replaced, and more than a hundred terms had no hit at all (print gallery,
autostereogram, flip dot, cochlea, varves, desert varnish, vocoder, image quilting, Wang tiles ...), which is where the
list was built. The photo is not decorated but sent through a named operator, and the operator's rules are the motion.

**The 100 transitions (`Tools/transgen`).** `tgen.py` takes the 100 sources (`drafts/Z1.txt` .. `Z8.txt`, a block per
transition with its mask or warp as a GLSL body and its metadata), wraps each in one template (the contract of
`Tools/SHADER_AUTHORING.md`, V12/V13: the endpoints exactly the two scenes, every helper term windowed with `sin(pi d)`,
geometry only on clocks from `time` and `audioAdvance`, the clock at about 1.2/255 per frame, the middle quiet, a breath of
`audioSwell` on the strength of the effect only), writes `Transitions/<Name>.frag` and registers them in `Komplett.xml`
(file, type, minFade, mood, probability, complexity, two knobs, speedP and hueP). `transheet.py` renders contact sheets
(five progress values, one job, below normal priority). Two thirds are slow or very slow (`calm`, `dreamy`), for Ambient,
SpaceAmbient, Downtempo and Cinematic, which had 29 usable transitions; they now have 75, 75, 81 and 89 (Ambient /
SpaceAmbient: 75 each).
- *Measured:* `PresetEditor --transcheck` (endpoints at most 1.5/255, jump = max step / median step at most 6) and
  `--transprofile` (the profile of every transition into `Tools/transition_profile.tsv`: total variation, the share of the
  change in the middle 80 % (`core80`), the peak step, flicker, flash). The soft genres need `core80 >= 0.45`, flash at most
  30, flicker at most 1.0, peak step at most 0.10 and no `wipe` / `blocky` mark; `make_genre_configs.py` refuses a transition
  without a profile row (the rows are named without `.frag`). 81 of the 100 passed at first (CrystalBallInversion, HueGateBleed,
  FlatAreasFirst and ShadowLiftCrossing stayed out of the soft genres until they were slowed down, see below), FireflyGlowHandoff (peak 0.37) is a harness artefact:
  the harness scene is nearly uniform, so a single bright wipe counts as a peak.
- *Rules found while tuning:* no `audioSpread` on a count or a scale (it moved the geometry of 20 transitions; amplitudes
  use `audioSwell` with the swell breath of the template); the order of random masks is made uniform (CDF remap) so the
  change is spread evenly over the progress; a mask taken from the photo needs a share of noise
  (`smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, fbm2)`), because on a nearly uniform scene a photo mask changes everything at one instant; tile and
  hex flips need a dimmed mix of both scenes behind them (black gaps otherwise).

**The 300 scenes (A to Y).** Families (number of scenes): A camera and sensor 12, B displays and printing technology 12,
C early cinema 12, D compression and coding 12, E data visualisation 12, F signals and telecommunications 12, G music
theory as space 12, H ear and instrument 12, I inlay and metalwork 12, J patterns of the world 12, K nonlinear dynamics 11,
L choice models and automata 13 (state fields), M plants under the microscope 12, N animal patterns without animals 12,
O geology II 12, P sky, sun and distance 12, Q granular matter, drops and threads 12, R solid state and quantum magnetism 12,
S paper, ink and hand printing 12, T texture synthesis 14, U line art and geometry of optimisation 12, V recursion and
perspective 12, W wavefronts and groups 12, X surfaces with wandering light 12, Y colour systems 10. 15 of them are state
fields (L, AntTrailStigmergyField, RulkovNeuronMapBursts); the other 285 render in one pass. Every scene has its operator
named in its `@brief`, its audio coupling in the doc block, and a knob (`sizeP` or `scaleP`) next to `hueP`.
- *Sizes are relative.* The contact sheets are 480 x 270, the app runs at 1080p and more, so every size in pixels is a
  constant per 270 lines times `resolution.y / 270.0` (a cell, a grain, a stripe); the mip level is computed from the base
  size, not from the scaled one. Without this the sheet and the app look different (grain 4 times finer, a flip-dot board with
  four times the dots). Round particles, no square pixel stars (the shake scan flags `floor(gl_FragCoord ...)` as PIXEL).
- *Music in the structure.* Counts, scales, rotations and cells follow only slow or integrated signals
  (`audioAdvance`, `audioHarmAdvance`, `audioSwell`, the phrase phase); the fast ones (Kick, Onset, Bass bands) only change
  brightness (the vocoder's band gains, the cochlea's four peaks at fixed places, the Helmholtz resonators' activation).
  Seamless loops by construction where an effect has one (the Risset rhythm is closed in `2^(k+f)`, and its ring pattern
  depends only on `k+f`; the Droste loop is a shear of the log radius).
- *Heavy ones.* The strange-attractor scenes (Chua, Roessler, Sprott, Rabinovich-Fabrikant) integrate six short trajectories
  per pixel (70 to 110 steps) and add the midpoints of the steps (without them the paths are chains of dots); the Duffing basin
  map runs 96 steps per pixel; Hofstadter's butterfly takes, per pixel, the nearest fraction p/q (q up to 16) and the trace of
  Harper's transfer matrices; the wireframe scan marches 64 steps over the photo as a height field.
- *State fields* (`//@state W H rate 32`, 32 bits): the cells carry the place of the photo they come from (g, b), so the
  picture is the photo at first and falls apart or sorts itself with the rule (Schelling, Potts, voter, traffic, the rules
  30 and 110 whose curtain falls one row a step at 44 steps a second). `PresetEditor --render` shows a state scene flat; the
  check is `ns_sample.py` (an app export of 14 to 16 seconds). Sznajd and the voter models end in consensus, so Sznajd has
  3 x 3 blocks of opinion flipped at random; the ant trails are a Keller-Segel pair (ant density climbs the pheromone gradient,
  with volume exclusion; without it the density collapses to points) and stay the weakest scene of the round.

**Traps of the round.**
- `fbm3(vec2)` is a three-octave 2-D noise, not a 3-D noise (the solid texture uses `fbm` with a rotating offset).
- A scene source with a local array initialised from non-constants is fine, but several `const` arrays in one function are
  not (the NVIDIA trap of the earlier rounds); the spectral locus is written as an `if` chain of `vec2`.
- `git add Presets/*.xml` fails on the ignored `ZZMesh.xml` / `ZZScreen01.xml`: name the eleven files.
- PowerShell 5.1 has no `Start-Process -PriorityClass`; start, then set `$p.PriorityClass = 'BelowNormal'`. The child
  processes (ffmpeg, the app) inherit it. While the user plays, every render ran as a single job at below normal priority.

**The close.**
- *Catalogue:* `render_catalog_export.py --list names300.txt --jobs 1 --chunk 60`: 900 frames of the 300 new scenes in 11.0
  minutes (one job, below normal priority); `make_catalog.py docs/Catalog/rendered/cat300b .../fxscan` kept the old images
  and added the new: 2475 scenes, 30 FX overlays, 210 transitions, 7703 images. `catalog_check.py` flagged four spatial
  rainbows (ChameleonIridophoreLattice, ColorSolidSliceCycle, PearlescentFlipFlopPaint, SpectralLocusRibbon); they are the
  point of their scene, so interest and galerie lost one step each instead of the scene.
- *Ratings:* the ratings given while building were above the old rows again (interest 6.40 against 5.36, galerie 7.04 against
  5.12, psychedelic 5.72 against 4.84, electronic 4.91 against 3.88, psytrance 4.99 against 3.91). The 300 were set to the old
  rows' level column by column (mean and spread, the spread stretched at most twice, the order inside the batch kept): galerie
  5.09, interest 5.80, psychedelic 4.83, electronic 3.91, psytrance 3.96.
- *Measured:* `screen.py --scenes <300>` (one recording of 302 windows): the new scenes cost 0.60 ms a frame at 1080p in the
  median, the dearest PolygonBokehBlades 1.77 ms, AutostereogramDepthDrift 1.44, VocoderBandBank 1.19, none above 3 ms; no
  new scene is flagged (22 old ones are, as before). The partial run overwrites `.screen/metrics.json`: back up
  `.screen/` first and fold the run back with `merge_screen.py <backup>` (5548 metric rows, 2475 costs).
  `sync_scene_measures.py` wrote gpuMs and the measured restlessness into `Komplett.xml` (many of the new scenes are calm:
  motion 0.01 to 0.02), `make_genre_configs.py` rebuilt the presets (Allround 2690 entries, Psychedelic 1011, Ambient 918,
  Club 705). `check_schedule.py --quick`: 20 plans, no violations.
- *Doxygen:* 113 warnings at first, all of them the scenes' own helper functions (and `phAt` / `stateStep` of the 15 state
  scenes); each has a block now (brief, `@param`, `@return`) in `Tools/scenegen/src/<Scene>.glsl`, written from a table
  and inserted before the definition; none now.

- *Genre membership, checked afterwards.* All 300 new scenes were in Allround and in at least one genre preset (one to six, two
  or three typically). Ten **old** scenes were in no genre preset (ChordRailwaySwitches, EmbroideryHoopStitches,
  FormantVowelSpace, KnittingRowsGrow, MarbleRunTrack, QuiltBlockPatchwork, SundialShadowSweep, TangramShuffle,
  WireworldCircuitry, XrayLuggageBelt): slow staged object scenes whose fit stayed below the take threshold in every column
  (`galerie` is not a genre) and two of them with interest 2 or below, which the dull filter drops. They now have fit 7 in two
  fitting genres each (calm ones Ambient / Downtempo, the celestial ones SpaceAmbient, the purple and colourful ones
  Psychedelic, the circuit and the scanner Electronic with Noir and Psychedelic) and interest at least 3. WireworldCircuitry
  is near black in all three catalogue frames; it is in Noir and Electronic now, but it stays a dark scene.
- *Transitions.* 29 of the 210 were in no genre preset: those tagged only `wipe` or `blocky` (the tags that keep a transition
  out of the calm genres) matched no mood rule anywhere else. `make_genre_configs.py` has `GEOMETRIC_GENRES` now: Club,
  Electronic and Psytrance take every `wipe` / `blocky` transition, Cinematic the wipes (still subject to the measured
  softness). Club has 117 transitions (was 63), Electronic 138 (89), Psytrance 132 (81), Cinematic 106 (89); the calm genres are
  unchanged (75, 75, 81). Four stayed in Allround alone at first: CrystalBallInversion, FlatAreasFirst, HueGateBleed and
  PolaroidDevelopSquare are tagged calm or dreamy but measured abrupt, so the calm genres refused them and the driving ones
  refuse the `calm` tag; they were slowed down afterwards (next point). `check_schedule.py --quick`: 20 plans, no violations.
- *The four slowed down (and a fifth).* Each failed a different test of the soft genres, so each got its own repair (profile before ->
  after, `--transprofile --scene Blit.frag`, endpoints unchanged in `--transcheck`):
  - PolaroidDevelopSquare (peak 0.139, flash 43.7 -> 0.057, 21.0): the card used to cover the old scene within the first
    seventh of the fade and was brighter than both scenes. The veil now grows over the first 42 %, the card and the milky
    sheet take their brightness from the two scenes (nine fixed points each, `meanLuma`), the clearing runs from the border
    over the whole depth of the picture instead of the outer 0.16 (the middle used to clear in one go), and the last blend
    to the new scene starts at 0.88 instead of 0.94.
  - CrystalBallInversion (core80 0.325, peak 0.103 -> 0.500, 0.043): the reversed picture used to turn upright through a
    zoom of factor 0, where the whole frame rushes by. It now turns by a half turn (the angle goes from pi to 0, the
    magnification from 1.8 to 1) and the ball grows with `d^0.7` instead of `sqrt(d)`. Its total variation is the largest of
    the soft ones (1145; a cross-fade is 55), so `minFade` rose from 6 to 8 s.
  - HueGateBleed (core80 0.425 -> 0.550): its order values pile up in the middle; `smoothstep(0, 1, f)` spreads them and the
    edge softness is 0.13 instead of 0.18 of a knob unit.
  - FlatAreasFirst (core80 0.400 -> 0.475): the roughness is taken as a share of the scene's typical roughness (four fixed
    points, `1 - exp(-r / mean)` under a square root), so a scene that is rough everywhere orders like one that is not, and the
    progress is warped by `d + 0.3 sin(2 pi d) / (2 pi)` (slower in the middle, faster at both ends). Without the
    normalisation the warp alone failed the jump test of `--transcheck` (9.2 against 6) on the moving harness scene.
  - ShadowLiftCrossing (core80 0.350 -> 0.550, flash 0 -> 17.1): the dark places of the scene have the order value 0 and
    all switched in the first third; the progress goes through `d^1.4` now (slow at the start, faster at the end).
  All five are in Ambient, SpaceAmbient, Downtempo and Cinematic now (80, 80, 86 and 111 transitions; Allround unchanged at 210). Two traps: `Start-Process -ArgumentList` with an array does not quote a path with a space (`--images` then
  silently falls back to the test card and every row of the profile differs; Crossfade must read 55.3), and an order value
  taken from the photo must be normalised against the scene, or the harness scene (still, smooth) and the moving one
  (rough everywhere) need opposite repairs.

**Release v1.19.0 (23.10.2026, tag on 7713bc82).** 2475 scenes, 210 transitions, 20 new labs and 40 chain classes with 100
variants each, the rebuilt audio analysis. The chain of v1.18 held, with these additions:
- `Tools/release_check.py --skip snapshots` (26 min of which chain 11, perf 6.5): three steps red. *analyzer*: novelty and the
  section threshold are in new units since the 22.10 rebuild (14 differences, nothing else), so `analyzer_regress.py --update`
  after looking at the list. *shaderdoc* and *layout*: the 100 generated transitions (`tgen.py build`) come out of the template
  with long comment lines and unaligned `uniform` comments; `doc_shaders.py`, then `cgvr_format.py` without `--check`, 101 files,
  whitespace only. A `tgen.py build` is always followed by these two.
- `deploy.ps1 -Build` rebuilds all four programs (Kaleidoscope, PresetEditor, SetupTool, ExportTool) and packs: 3.5 min, ZIP
  43.6 MB, Setup 24.2 MB, 3508 entries. The portable ZIP, unpacked into a fresh folder, ran one export per genre preset
  without a FATAL or a shader error (30 s of `review128.wav`, 640 x 360).
- **The catalogue PDF**: Chrome dies with exit code `0xE0000008` (out of memory) on the single page of 2475 scenes, with and
  without `--user-data-dir`. `Tools/print_catalog_pdf.py` prints five parts of about 540 entries (5 s each) and joins them with
  Ghostscript: 1002 pages, 73 MB. The one catalogue image that changed (PolaroidDevelopSquare) was rendered again with
  `render_catalog_images.ps1 -Kind trans`, then `make_catalog.py "" docs/Catalog/rendered/fxscan`.

## 10.11.2026 (66): after the release -- selection, a repaired measuring instrument, tempo, the first impression

Asked whether there was still room for improvement, five points were named and then worked through. What each
turned out to be is not always what was claimed beforehand; where the claim was wrong it says so.

### 1. Selection instead of quantity

- *The viewer's verdicts that exist are no ratings.* The settings file holds 307 taste weights, all of them skips,
  221 from the test bench `TestAlle` walked from A to C; no favourite, no ban. So there was nothing to fold back yet.
  The way back exists now: `Tools/apply_taste.py` turns the weights the app learns per preset and scene (skip x 0.8,
  favourite x 1.25, ban) into `Tools/user_taste.tsv`, steps on that genre's fit column (Allround: interest), which
  `make_genre_configs.py` applies. One skip is not a verdict (people skip to look around); two are a step down.
  Benches and presets that no longer exist are ignored. Five corrections came out of the present file.
- *The dull tail.* A quarter of the 2474 rated scenes stood at interest 4 or less, and since the plan walks through
  all scenes of a preset before one returns, a dull scene comes as often as the best. `DULL` went from 2 to 3: the
  185 scenes rated 3 (looked at as contact sheets: flat, murky or nearly empty in all three frames; six that look
  fine were raised to 4) are in no genre preset any more, Allround keeps them. Scenes rated 4 or less: Noir 43 ->
  31 %, Ambient 21 -> 15 %, Electronic 20 -> 17 %. This takes back a part of "every scene has a home" (22.10.);
  `DULL = 2` restores it.
- *Measured candidates are suspects, not verdicts.* How much of the frame a scene fills (pixels above 0.10 in the
  catalogue frames) singles out the light-on-black scenes: 123 fill less than a fifth. They are neon lines, particles
  and objects on black -- a look, not a defect, and at home in SpaceAmbient and Noir -- so no rule was made of it.
  The screening's brightness ratio loud / quiet (`hot_vs_quiet`) is no measure of reactivity either: a scene that
  answers the music with its geometry reads 1.0.

### 2. The audio analysis

- *Correction of the claim "16 of 30 drops".* The other 14 cue drops have no bass return (62); the detector is at
  what can be heard. The gap was the tempo.
- *Measured anew* (`Tools/tempo_vs_cues.py`, `Tools/analyser_cue_set.txt` = the 43 demos; the reference is the median
  interval of the cues' beats within 4 s): right within 4 % in 39 % of the rhythmic time, 71 % at 90..135 BPM, 75 %
  above, 14 % below 90 BPM. Below 90 the analyser reads the double by design (it folds every tempo into 70..180:
  a pulse at the double is on the grid), so "on the grid" (right, double or half) is the fairer number: 61 %.
- *The two sources, logged per block* (`AudioFeatures::tempoAc`, `tempoKick` and their confidences, in
  `PresetEditor --features`): the kick intervals alone are right in 17 % of the time, the autocorrelation alone in
  50 % -- yet below a confidence of 0.35 the kicks set the tempo, and they pulled at it on every kick. Replaying
  rules on the logged sources: letting the autocorrelation lead at any confidence gains 6 points, the kicks' metres
  2 and 1/2 turn more right tempos into octave errors than the reverse, the 2:3 is wrong whenever it fires, the 3:2
  pays only where the kicks explain 95 % of their intervals (a clean two-step).
- *The rule now:* the kicks set the tempo until the autocorrelation has one; then the autocorrelation leads (followed
  in 0.1 s when confident, in 2 s when not), times 1.5 where clean kicks sit at 3:2. Measured: right 39 -> 49 %, folded
  43 -> 55 %, on the grid 61 -> 69 %, at 90..135 BPM 71 -> 81 %. Real tracks, share of the time within 4 % of the
  true tempo: Astrix 64 -> 97 %, Daft Punk 61 -> 100 %, DMT 74 -> 94 %, Kadafi 42 -> 80 %, Prodigy 12 -> 97 % (130; it
  read 106..112), Thunderstruck 69 -> 100 %. *Worse:* Ironic 48 -> 25 %; it reads its dotted pulse (171 for 114) in
  61 % of the time, where the kicks used to hold it near 116..124 for half of it. (The commit message of the change
  gives shares of 2-BPM bins, which are smaller.) Sections and drops unchanged (125 of 281, 16 of 30); self-test 127 of 127.
- *Tried and dropped:* letting the double lag support a lag (Ellis' duple weighting) against the dotted readings:
  81 -> 84 % at 90..135 BPM but 78 -> 54 % above 135 -- in the 4-s window three beats of a fast track correlate as
  well as two.

### 3. The measuring instrument of the transitions was blind on one eye

- *The outgoing scene was one flat colour.* `--transprofile --scene Blit.frag` was meant as "a still photo", but
  `Engine/Blit.frag` reads `tex` at `vUV`, which the preview does not feed: one texel. Everything a transition does
  to the OLD picture (a slide, a fold, a pixelation, a spin) was invisible, and a veil was measured against a dark
  grey. `Engine/ProfileStill.frag` shows the photo. A cross-fade reads 58.27 now (55.30).
- *The table was stale as well:* the rows of 96 of the 100 generated transitions did not match their shaders (measured
  before the last tuning on 23.10.; the tell: every flash 0.0). On the flat colour several veils flashed far above
  both scenes (snow 110, mist 83).
- *Pinned:* `PresetEditor --transprofile --photos A,B` names the two photos (it took the first two of `Images/`, so a
  library that grows moves every row) and refuses a folder without photos (a path with a blank passed unquoted used
  to measure the test card silently); `--only A,B` for the loop of change and measure.
  `Tools/transition_profile.py` runs profile and jump test, checks the cross-fade's value, merges rows by name: five
  transitions in five seconds. `release_check.py` has the step `transitions` (33 s).
- *`SOFT_FLICK` 1.0 -> 1.25:* the clock-driven change is measured on the whole frame now, about 1.27 times the old
  numbers. PoincareSpin (2.12) is out of the calm genres: it spins the old picture.
- *Veils in the scenes' light* (`trVeil()` in the template): fog, snow, gauze, pollen and foam were fixed light
  greys mixed in up to 92 %. Their colour is dimmed until it is at most 0.09 above the brighter scene's mean
  (nine fixed points each). Snow 110 -> 28, mist 83 -> 25, fog 62 -> 21, pollen 65 -> 21, gauze 46 -> 6.
- *A progress curve from the measurement* (`Tools/transition_warp.py`): a transition that does its work in a third
  of its progress is a jolt at any length. The tool measures where the change sits and writes the inverse of its
  cumulative as a monotone cubic through 17 knots (`evenProgress(d)`, endpoints exact, never backwards; 85 % of the way
  to an even spread, two passes; a stretch without change keeps some time). For a generated transition the knots
  live in the draft (`warp:`), or the next build would lose them. Fitted on the flat colour it made five sliding
  transitions worse (jump up to 56: it skipped what it could not see); on the photo it holds. Re-timed: LatentDenoise-
  Arrival (jump 20.3 -> 1.9, core80 0.35 -> 0.78), SpinodalDecomposition (17.5 -> 1.1), Pixelation, LeidenfrostSkitter,
  ScratchboardReveal, SeamCarvingRetarget, GoldenNautilus (6.2 -> 2.5), WaveFunctionCollapseTiles, FlatAreasFirst,
  SandVeilPassing, TideLineWashSand.
- *An order taken from the picture is normalised, not re-timed:* Luminance (keys around the scenes' mean
  brightness, stretched and spread: core80 0.30 -> 0.53); a curve fitted on one photo fails the jump test on
  another scene (13.0).
- *Result:* all 210 pass the jump test (seven failed), 187 pass the soft limits; Ambient has 84 transitions (80),
  Cinematic 116 (111). `tgen.py build` runs `doc_shaders.py` and `cgvr_format.py` over what it built. All 210 have
  their catalogue frames (the 100 new ones had none).
- *A mistake on the way:* `git checkout -- drafts/Z1.txt` to undo one edit threw away the uncommitted veil and
  curve edits of that file; they were recovered from the built shaders (the knots are in the `K[17]` array). Commit
  before undoing, or undo by hand.

### 4. The first impression

- *CI had been red since v1.18*, the release commit of v1.19.0 included. Three causes: `shadercheck.py` compiles
  every shader with the real driver since rule C1, and the runner's default OpenGL knows no GLSL 3.30 (all 3200
  "did not compile"); the static part runs first now (`--no-compile`), the compile after Mesa is installed. Eight of
  twelve ShipDocking entries had no `spinAxisP` (`PresetEditor --validate`; 0 = X, what they did). The build ran the
  packaging, whose Inno Setup rejects `installer.iss` on the runner (`RunDeploy=false`).
- *What Mesa's compiler found:* four scenes with variables named `active`, `cast` and `mat2` -- reserved words and a
  type name that NVIDIA lets pass. On Linux with Mesa these scenes did not compile. Renamed. The compile of every
  shader with Mesa is a gate now (it runs whenever Mesa could be installed on the runner; the jump test under Mesa
  stays informational): the only check with a second GLSL compiler.
- *Release notes* of v1.19.0 in English, the German text folded below. *README:* a moving picture at the top
  (`Tools/make_demo_clip.py`: eight scenes in one video export, an animated WebP of 480 x 270).

### 5. The catalogue as a page

- `docs/Catalog/index.html` + `catalog-data.js` (written by `make_catalog.py`): 2715 entries, search over names and
  descriptions, filters by kind, genre preset and mood, the three frames and the full text on a click. Static, no
  dependency, works from the disk. Hearts and crosses are kept in the browser and exported as a TSV for
  `apply_taste.py --ratings` -- the cheap way to the ratings point 1 lacks.
- *The weight was overestimated.* The repository is 173 MB on GitHub, the catalogue frames 86 MB of the tree at 11 KB
  a frame. Moving them out would not shrink the history without rewriting it, which is not worth its risk. Nothing
  was moved.

### Tools and traps

- Snapshot sets name their photo (`photo.txt`; it was "the middle one of `Images/`" on every run). The baseline is
  `2026-11-10-all`: the set of 23.10. plus the 300 scenes it lacked; two old scenes re-rendered with the named photo
  are identical to it.
- A here-document in this shell eats one backslash even when quoted: `"\\n"` in an inline Python patch becomes a line
  break in the patched file (three times that day). Patch scripts with backslashes go into a file first.
- `Start-Process -ArgumentList '-File x.ps1 -Names A,B'` passes `A,B` as ONE name; `-Command "& 'x.ps1' -Names A,B"`
  passes a list.

**The catalogue page online (10.11.2026).** https://reneweller-coding.github.io/KaleidoscopeEnhanced/ -- GitHub Pages with
the source "GitHub Actions"; `.github/workflows/pages.yml` publishes `docs/Catalog` and nothing else (the page reads
its data and pictures by relative paths, so the folder is the site), whenever the catalogue changes on master.
- The Pages side needs five to ten minutes to sync the 7,906 files (69 MB as an artifact). The first deployment sat in
  `syncing_files` until the action's default limit of ten minutes; the next one took six. The step has 25 minutes now.
- A failed deployment is started anew (`gh workflow run Pages --ref master`), not re-run: the re-run uploads a second
  artifact named `github-pages` into the same run and the deployment refuses two.

**Release v1.19.1 (10.11.2026, tag on 349a0c56).** What (66) changed, for the people who download: tempo, the re-timed
and re-lit transitions, the tighter genre presets, the four scenes repaired for Mesa.
- `Tools/release_check.py --skip snapshots`: green in all steps on the first run, 21.5 min (chain 672 s, perf 388 s,
  doxygen 106 s, the new step `transitions` 36 s).
- `deploy.ps1 -Build`: 4.7 min (Inno Setup needed two retries for the antivirus lock), ZIP 43.6 MB, Setup 24.2 MB, 3509
  entries. Unpacked into a fresh folder, with an empty settings file: one export of 8 s with each of the twelve
  presets, no FATAL, no shader error.
- `Katalog.pdf`: 1021 pages, 79 MB, every one of the 210 transitions with its two pictures. Joining the parts took
  most of the five minutes this time.
- The notes are in English with the German text folded below, as v1.19.0's are now. Eleven transitions carry the
  progress curve (`evenProgress`), Luminance is normalised instead.

## 20.11.2026 (67): the plan of 20.11. -- tempo and beat, how the scenes answer the music, look-alikes, the transitions in the catalogue, Linux, stereo, memory over hours

`docs/PLAN_2026-11-20.md` in one go: blocks A to H as the user decided them on 20.11. (H2 stereo, D4 AppImage and B5
near-duplicates yes; projector correction H1, VR H3 and room light no; the demo video comes from the user, the
catalogue page only has its slot).  Built partly in worktrees (`kaleido-wt\{linux,catalog,ui,sim,b2}`, all merged).
What each package did and what it measured:

| package | what | result |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | the tempo moved into `Source/TempoTracker.{h,cpp}`; a trace (`--tempo-trace`) and a lab (`Tools/tempo_lab.py`) | features and traces of 82 files byte-identical before and after |
| A1 | a yardstick for the beat phase (`Tools/beat_vs_cues.py`: F-measure, CMLt, AMLt, hold) | baseline of the PLL: F 27.5 %, CMLt 20.7 %, AMLt 28.0 %, hold 26 % (chance 25 %) |

The packages follow, each as it was written down when it was done.

### Block A -- tempo and beat (A0-A3)

The plan (docs/PLAN_2026-11-20.md) began with the tempo: right within 4 % in 49 % of the rhythmic time of the 43
annotated demos, and the beat phase never measured at all.

- *A lab first* (`Tools/tempo_lab.py`).  `PresetEditor --features ... --tempo-trace FILE` writes, for every 10-ms block,
  what the tempo sees and what it published (`AudioAnalyzer::M_TempoTrace`, 14 float32: the SuperFlux samples, the
  kick and its interval, track change, the autocorrelation's tempo and confidence, the published tempo and phase, the
  kick tempo and its explained share), and three new feature columns `beat_phase`, `beat_phase_c` (the conditioner's
  PLL, what the shaders see) and `beats`.  The lab replays a method in Python on those inputs and scores it exactly
  like `tempo_vs_cues.py`: 37 s per method (10 s with four workers) instead of a build and minutes of analysis.  The
  port of the method of 10.11. matched the C++ in every demo (no demo with more than 1 % of its blocks off by
  0.5 BPM) and reproduced the table to the percent.  `--real` scores seven real tracks against `Tools/tempo_truth.tsv`
  (the values come from the analyser's medians and a whole-track autocorrelation where both agree; Ironic's 84 the
  user gave from official sources -- at first it stood at 114, taken from a note; the other six are unconfirmed),
  `--calm` the confidence on nine calm tracks (three
  Noctuary renders, five additive-synth demos, the chord test track).
- *A0, the move.*  The autocorrelation and the fusion with the kicks went into `Source/TempoTracker.{h,cpp}` unchanged:
  the feature files and traces of the 41 beat demos and the seven real tracks (82 files) were byte-identical before
  and after, analyzer_regress as the baseline, self test 127 of 127.  All inputs are known before the old
  autocorrelation section, and nothing between it and the fusion read the tempo, so one `update()` per block keeps
  the order.
- *A1, a yardstick for the phase* (`Tools/beat_vs_cues.py`).  F-measure (+-70 ms), CMLt and AMLt after Davies, Degara &
  Plumley 2009 (the definitions of mir_eval), for the kicks, the analyser's phase and the PLL, plus "hold": annotated
  beats inside stretches of 8 s or more without a kick, phase within an eighth of a beat.  Baseline over 25,034 beats:
  the PLL F 27.5 %, CMLt 20.7 %, AMLt 28.0 %, hold 26 % -- chance is 25 %.
- *A2, the tempo by pulse trains* (`TempoTracker::choose()`).  Candidates: the strongest five peaks of the
  autocorrelation over the last 12 s and their x2, /2, x3/2, x2/3; each scored by a pulse train laid over the onset
  envelope at its best phase -- how far the envelope at the pulses stands above its mean over all phases (Percival &
  Tzanetakis 2014) -- plus 0.3 x the trains at twice and half the period, times the old prior around 120 BPM.  The
  gate (peak, prominence, kurtosis of the 4-s window) is untouched.  Tried in the lab: the plain pulse train (64 %
  right but Astrix 97 -> 88 %, Ironic 28 -> 0: they switched to their 3:4 and dotted readings), half-beat pulses,
  an 8-s window, only binary relatives, no prior, a wider prior, without the kicks' 3:2 (identical on the demos),
  margins 1.15/1.25/1.35, multi-level weights 0.3/0.5.  Kept: multi-level 0.3, and a reading outside the 4-s pick's
  octave family must score 1.25 times as high.  Measured (tempo_vs_cues.py): right 49 -> 66 %, 90..135 BPM 81 -> 87 %,
  over 135 78 -> 80 %, under 90 25 -> 51 % (on the beat grid 60 -> 69 %, A4: the fold stays), folded 55 -> 74 %.
  Real tracks: Astrix 97 -> 98, Daft Punk 100, DMT 92, Kadafi 80 -> 93, Prodigy 97 -> 100, Thunderstruck 100.
  Ironic first read *worse* (28 -> 14 %) -- against a reference of 114 BPM taken from a note.  Every source reads
  171 or 86 there (the autocorrelation, the pulse trains, the kick intervals), and the official tempo is 84 (the
  user, 20.11.): against 84 the old method is right 12 % of the time, the new one 85 %.  Calm material: the
  confidence exactly as before (the gate is the
  same).  Features run 4.6 s (4.8 before).  self test 127/127, check_schedule 20 plans without a violation.
- *A3, the beat phase by beat tracking* (`TempoTracker::beatStep()`).  The phase restarted at every kick and ran at the
  tempo in between: a syncopated kick moved it off the beat, a break let it drift.  Now BTrack's cumulative score and
  predicted beat (Stark, Davies & Plumley 2009) on the SuperFlux envelope and the published tempo, with the paper's
  constants (alpha 0.9, tightness 5); tap tempo and the external clock still win.  A second lab
  (`Tools/beat_lab.py`) replays phase methods and the conditioner's PLL in Python (the PLL model matches the C++ column
  in all but 0.07 % of the blocks; the C++ build reproduces the lab to the digit).  Through the PLL: F 27.9 -> 48.5 %,
  CMLt 25.8 -> 43.8 %, AMLt 32.9 -> 61.1 %; hold 25 -> 39 % -- better than chance, but not "held", which the plan asked
  for.  Tightness 2 and 3 measured within two points.  No pulse on calm material (the conditioner's beat pulse equal or
  lower on all nine calm tracks).  One baseline change accepted: broadband120's conditioned beat pulse p90 0.718 ->
  0.645 (the PLL's pulse now falls on the kicks instead of between them).
  *A slip on the way:* the first lab version predicted the next beat right after a beat instead of half a beat later;
  it looked as if a lead of 80 ms helped (F 40.8 %).  With BTrack's scheduling no lead is needed (48.6 %), and the
  same lead on the old kick phase made it worse (27.9 -> 22.7 %) -- the gain was the tracker's, the "lead" only
  repaired the slip.
  *Counted in envelope samples since* (after the crash of section 67, fix): the first version stepped once per
  analysis block and took the period in blocks, and live a block is whatever the capture hands over -- a 1-ms
  WASAPI packet made the period 500 blocks and overran `predictBeat()`'s scratch.  Now `pushOnset()` keeps the
  block's envelope samples and `update()` steps the tracker once per sample (100 Hz), the period in samples (at most
  86 at 70 BPM); the phase is taken from the block's start time as before, the clamp stays as a guard.  Offline a
  block holds exactly one sample, so nothing measured moved: `beat_lab.py --method trace` again F 48.5 %, CMLt
  43.8 %, AMLt 61.1 %, hold 39 %; `tempo_lab.py --check` 66 % right and 0 of 41 demos off the port; self test 137
  of 137 with the 1-ms packets of check 7.
- *A5, section boundaries on the bar grid -- tried and dropped.*  The idea: with a trustworthy phase, a novelty
  peak near a phrase boundary counts more.  Re-simulated from the per-block novelty and the conditioner's 8-bar
  phrase position on the 43 demos (scored like `analyser_vs_cues.py`): a lower threshold near the phrase boundary
  and a higher one elsewhere found more boundaries (best: 48 -> 53 %, Groove 37 -> 42 %) but always invented more as
  well (58 -> 58..74 %), and the plan forbade more false alarms.  The re-simulation itself over-triggers against the
  real detector (it lacks the absolute-novelty floor: 136 found, 180 invented, against the analyser's 125 and 132),
  so not even its gain is certain.  The detector stays as it is (sections 44 % found, 52 % invented, Groove 31 %).
  Timing was never the bottleneck: a boundary counts as found 2 s before to 6 s after it, and the detector fires
  within about two seconds; what it misses, it misses because the novelty stays below its threshold.

### B1 -- how much each scene answers the music

The screening's numbers could not say it (66): the brightness ratio loud/quiet reads 1.0 for a scene that answers
with its geometry.  `Tools/reactivity.py` renders every scene twice by the video export on the frame clock, with the
same seed and parameter rolls -- once over the screening music (chord bed, lead, bass and drums at 128 BPM, loud and
quiet halves of an 8-s cycle), once over silence of the same length -- and compares the two.  Whatever differs, the
music did.

- `react_struct`: each frame normalised to zero mean and unit spread, the mean absolute difference music against
  silence (0 = the same picture, about 1.1 = unrelated pictures) -- brightening alone reads near 0.
- `react_sync`: the change the music adds from frame to frame (the music run's frame difference minus the silent
  run's) against the music's onset envelope, Pearson, best of lags 0..3 frames.
- `react`: the rank of the mean of both ranks, 0..1 (the catalogue page shows it as a badge).
- *The controls.*  No scene of the catalogue is free of audio (every scene reacts, by the house rules), so the still side
  was made: the photo itself as a scene (`Engine/ProfileStill.frag`) and null pairs -- ten heavily reactive scenes
  rendered silence against silence.  The null pairs read exactly 0.000 (the export is deterministic), the photo 0.16
  (the engine's own small answer), the ten reactive scenes 0.32..0.82: a clean separation.
- *Two traps found on the way.*  Photo changes fall on the music's phrases, so with free photos the two runs showed
  different pictures and the static photo read 1.06 -- the photo is fixed now (`KALEIDO_FIXED_PHOTO`, the snapshot
  baseline's).  And a scene's own periodic motion correlated with the 4-s loud/quiet cycle by chance (a null pair
  read a sync of 0.29), so the sync uses the music run's change minus the silent run's.
- *The run.*  2,474 of 2,475 scenes in 52 minutes (480 x 270 at 15 fps, 8 s per scene, 0.8 s per scene and run;
  TunnelPlain fell into a sacrificial window).  react_struct p5 0.14, median 0.45, p95 0.83; 160 scenes stay below
  the static photo's 0.16; react_sync is 0 for 129.  The two measures are nearly independent (r = -0.15).
- *Against the ratings.*  interest and react: rank correlation 0.12 -- the ratings came from contact sheets, which
  cannot show an answer to music.  25 scenes rated 7 or 8 sit in the bottom 5 % (KlimtGoldMosaic, RooftopRainTokyo,
  StarshipPlanetaryOrbit, KardashevTypeIIICity, ApollonianSpherePackingGasket, ...), 17 rated 3 or 4 in the top 5 %
  (KolmogorovMeanders, RockPaperScissorsSpirals, BeeWaggleDance, ...).  Contact sheets "with music / with silence" of
  the bottom 5 % (124 scenes, react < 0.05) are in `.screen/reactivity/sheets`; for most of them the two halves look
  the same.  Only 8 of the 124 are 3D scenes (13 % of the catalogue is 3D).

### B2 -- music into the structure of the least reactive scenes, the rest sorted

Plan 20.11.2026, package B2.

#### What was found

- *Input:* the bottom 5 % of `Tools/scene_reactivity.tsv` (B1): 124 scenes below react 0.050, 25 of them rated
  interest 7 or 8. Each was looked at on the B1 contact sheets (music left, silence right) and in its source.
- *The measure moves with the scene's place in its set.* `Tools/reactivity.py --scenes` renders the names in sorted
  order, and the rolls under `KALEIDO_SEED`, the analyser's state and the encoder's noise depend on that place. One
  set measured twice gives the same numbers (three untouched controls repeated to 0.003), but the same scene in
  another set does not: KardashevTypeIIICity read react 0.018 in B1, 0.261 and 0.002 in two other sets (its sync
  0.14 / 0.43 / 0.09; its struct 0.08 every time). Sync is the noisy half: for a scene the music does not touch, the
  music run's extra frame difference is encoder noise, and its correlation with the onsets is anything from 0 to 0.4.
  Hence every before/after below is one set measured twice, at the base commit (3927e55a) and with the change.
- *Two more readings of the untouched scenes* (`all124base`: all 117 measurable ones in one go; `rest3`: the 73 left
  after the changes): 48 of 117 stayed below 0.05 in the second reading; with the median of the three readings, 46 of
  the 73 left are below 0.05 and 27 above (B1's low value was the position).
- *Why they were deaf -- the numbers of the screening music.* A probe scene that drew the uniforms as bars
  (bar heights survive the exposure and the encoder; grey levels did not) gave, per 8-s window of the screening WAV
  (4 s loud, 4 s quiet): `sceneAdvance` about 0.3-0.4 (0.05 a second), `audioPhase` about 2.5 rad, `audioHarmAdvance`
  about 1.2 on the chord bed, `audioSwell` 0 -> 1 in the loud half and back to 0.1-0.3, the kick only in the loud half.
  In silence all of them stand. The generated scenes ran their clocks as `0.03 * audioAdvance + 0.03 * sceneTime`:
  the music carried about 5 % of the motion, the swell a size, the kick nothing. The hand-made ones flew and turned
  on `sceneTime + 0.4 * sceneAdvance` (2 %), and several were still lifes with the music only in the light
  ("Nothing moves but the light", KlimtGoldMosaic's header).
- *The machine's media session got into the measurement.* The app asks the system what it plays (`NowPlaying`) and
  weaves title, lyrics and artist into the picture -- in the video export too. The final set, measured once while a
  track played on this machine and once with `KALEIDO_NP_FAKE` (a scripted session that never names a track), read
  up to 0.19 apart in struct or sync; two runs with the scripted session agree to 0.0005. `Tools/screen.py` (and so
  `reactivity.py`) and `Tools/scene_snapshots.py` now set it themselves. The numbers of the decisions below are from
  clean runs; the second and third readings of the untouched scenes (`all124base`, `rest3`) may carry it -- a fourth,
  clean one (`rest_np`) differs from `rest3` by 0.075 react on average. When B1 ran is not known to me; if something
  played overnight, B1 carries it too.
- *Blind spots of the measure:* it looks at 160 x 90. Patterns finer than that (SphericalWaveCrossStitch's
  interference stitches, 2-6 px at 1080p) or a mask moving over a fixed photo (PaisleyBotehDrift's drops turned,
  their photo did not) hardly register. The mesh scenes need the model pack (`Models/`, not in the worktree): the
  seven of them were judged on the B1 sheets and the B1 value alone.

#### How the music went in

- *The clock re-weighted:* the scene's own clock keeps 40-60 % of its rate, and an integrated music term is added
  that carries most of the motion while music plays -- e.g. `0.012 * sceneTime + 0.6 * sceneAdvance` for
  `0.03 * audioAdvance + 0.03 * sceneTime`: with music about the old speed, in silence a creep, never a stop.
  Positions and flights ride `sceneAdvance` (per activation, small, never jumps), turns and ripples `audioPhase`,
  changes that belong to the harmony `audioHarmAdvance`, sizes, depths and thresholds `audioSwell` (seconds), and the
  kick is light only -- on crests, rims, seams, top faces, glows, never on the frame.
- *Scenes with a state pass:* the swell scales the step of the integrator (AllenCahnCoarsening,
  DifferentialGrowthFolds, PhotoGapFingering): loud music drives the growth on, silence lets it rest -- a true
  integrator, not a speed multiplied into a clock.
- *Cameras stay on their clocks* where the scene is a view of an object: StarshipPlanetaryOrbit's planet turns on the
  music, the camera above it keeps `time`; FusorStarMode's cage turns, the eye does not. Flights that were already
  on `audioAdvance` moved to `sceneAdvance` with a larger share (ApollonianSpherePackingGasket, HistogramTerrainFlight,
  SupermassiveBlackHoleOrbit's orbit).
- *Found on the way:* VoronoiSpinBlur passed its clock to a function that never used it (the scene was a still photo
  with a swell-dependent blur); GongShimmerBloom's two nodal modes ran on `t` and `1.1 t`, so the hand-over at each
  wrap of the mode index jumped -- one clock now; FatouParabolicFlowers computed its harmony value and never used it;
  StarshipPlanetaryOrbit's cloud deck scaled its weather by `audioBass`, a fast signal on a spatial scale that makes
  the whole field shiver -- `audioSwell` now (OrbitalRingStation has the same line; its change was dropped, see
  below, so it is still there).
- *Generated scenes* were changed in `Tools/scenegen/src/<Name>.glsl` and rebuilt one by one
  (`gen.py <Name>`). Rebuilt unchanged, 19 of the 85 generated scenes of the list differ from their committed file
  (functions added to the libraries since -- famExpose() in the colour-family library, stCarry/stUV/stLod in the
  state library -- and "0..1" in knob comments); nine of them are among the changed ones (ChihulyPersianCeiling,
  DifferentialGrowthFolds, FatouParabolicFlowers, FusorStarMode, LoneStarQuilt, MoireReveal, OilCellKaleidoscope,
  PhytoplanktonSpirals, WaterRippleProjector) and carry that drift now: an uncalled famExpose() and comments, checked
  by rebuilding each one's base source with today's generator. No other scene was rebuilt.

#### Decisions

124 scenes: **(a) 50** got the music into their structure; **(b) 26** are calm by nature and stay as they are, with
club, electronic and psytrance capped at 2 in `Tools/preset_fit.tsv` (ambient raised to 6 or space to 7 where needed);
**(c) 35** are weak and go to Allround only (every genre column capped at 2, interest unchanged); **13** read above
the threshold in both re-measurements and stay untouched.

**(a)** -- one set of all 50, measured at the base commit and with the change (both without the machine's media
session, see Open), each ranked against the B1 table (the other rows unchanged). Before: 0.002 .. 0.451, median
0.064, 20 below 0.050. After: 0.093 .. 0.979, median 0.447, none below; measured twice, the two runs agree to
0.0005.

#### Open

- *The measure's position noise.* A scene's react depends on its place in the set (rolls, the analyser's state,

- *The mesh scenes* were not re-measured (no model pack in the worktree); their decisions rest on the B1 sheet and
